sector.narrative: Support for feminist, women-led and women's rights organisations and movements, and institutions (governmental and non-govermental) at all levels to enhance their effectiveness, influence and substainability (activities and core-funding). These organisations exist to bring about transformative change for gender equality and/or the rights of women and girls in developing countries. Their activities include agenda-setting, advocacy, policy dialogue, capacity development, awareness raising and prevention, service provision, conflict-prevention and peacebuilding, research, organising, and alliance and network building

YWLs will attend different events and meetings and holdstate duty bearers accountable.

On November 6, research findings sharing meeting held with local government in Kaukhali sub-district. During the meeting the Officer-in-Charge of Kaukhali Police Station commented inappropriately about sex workers and hold women accountable to some extent in occurring SGBV. YWL Sharmin Sultana courageously challenged his comment mentioning about sex workers’ profession and rights and shared her experience about working for SGBV victims. In the same meeting YWL Sharmila Ray Brishti has pointed on mismanagement of Kaukhali Upazila Health Complex and doctors’ partial treatment towards general patients preferring specific diagnostic centres. She mentioned the specific doctor’s name and shared her experience while receiving services. On 17 November YWL Malobika Azim has attended Upazila monthly NGO coordination and monitoring meeting in Tahirpur Upazila. The meeting was organized to strengthen coordination among the NGOs and follow-up their activities. 9 YWLs from 5 project implementing areas have attended national roundtable meeting jointly organized by Prothom Alo and Naripokkho with policy makers and highlighted issues regarding SGBV, SRHR and communal harmony in their locality.This year, YWL Sengchi Areng was honoured with the “Jayita” award in recognition of her outstanding efforts to improve the lives of girls and women in her community. •On June one of Halima’s relatives have visit her home from village and shared about domestic violence she had been through by her husband and in laws. YWL Halima took her to nearby Pallabi police station and complained about the domestic violence case. The respective police officer told that as the incident occurs in another area so they can’t take the case. Then Halima insisted and urged that the victim is from the camp, her parents live here and now she is living here with her parents and her in-laws are threatening her, so in this situation some action must be taken. Then they filed a general diary (GD) on the case.•On 21 July in project closing meeting at Kaukhali, Pirojpur YWL Reshma highlighting that due to syndicate they have got harassed while going to Pirojpur booking 3 easy bikes. So, if the concerned authority looks after the matter many passengers won’t get harassed further by the syndicate

4 talk shows organized and hosted by YWLs from Kaukhali, Tahirpur, Kalshi and Dhobaura have been broadcasted on local TV and you tube channels- Pirojpur TV on 29 February, Dainik Sunamganjer Khobor on1 April, BD Garo Production YouTube channel on 20th September and Channel Muskan YouTube channel on 27th November- featuring the active participation of Head teacher, Assistant teacher of government primary schools, Upazilla Youth Development Officer, former UP member and present women member, village council chairman and vice chairman, Medical Officer from Upazilla health complex, renowned gynecologist from Kurmitola General Hospital, women’s rights activist, social and cultural activist, indigenous female volunteer activists, and General Secretary and Organizing Secretary of the Stranded People’s General Rehabilitation Committee (SPJRC). The discussion centered on Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) and the current state of women’s rights activism. On 3 December, Naripokkho and Prothom Alo hosted the national roundtable “Narir Egiye Chola: Badha O Uttoroner Upay” (Women Gaining Ground: Obstacles and a Way Forward). Panelists, including policymakers, women’s rights activists, and researchers, discussed SGBV, women’s health, SRHR, and communal harmony, presenting practical solutions. The findings were published in Prothom Alo.
